_what_this_is: Three voices for three rooms of the out-patients wing. Materials in this world's language; every horizontal anchor is the wall handrail at 0.90 m.

handrail.line: the continuous wall handrail above the floor
handrail.sentence: A clearly legible continuous wood-effect PVC handrail with a rounded profile runs corner to corner at exactly 0.90 m above the floor, on every exposed wall surface including the side-wall returns, interrupted only by the doorway.
handrail.label: HANDRAIL 0.90 M ABOVE FLOOR - GATE ANCHOR
handrail.why: This wing's universal anchor: every room carries the building's wall handrail at one height, on every wall. A painter draws it and the instrument finds it.

reception_public.why: The waiting area is the wing's public face: it was decorated once, in a colour scheme, and has been scuffed at hip height ever since.
reception_public.walls: pale mint painted plaster above the handrail; below it, grey-green wipeable wall-protection sheet with a dark grey vinyl skirting, scuffed along the sitting line
reception_public.ceiling: a suspended grid of white mineral-fibre ceiling tiles with recessed fluorescent light panels
reception_public.floor: mottled grey-blue sheet vinyl with welded seams, coved up the wall at the skirting
reception_public.blank: unbroken grey-green wall-protection sheet below the handrail with pale mint painted plaster above

treatment_clinical.why: The treatment room is washed down daily: everything on its walls is a sheet that can be wiped, and its light is the flattest in the wing.
treatment_clinical.walls: white glossy antibacterial wall-cladding sheets with welded joints below the handrail; satin white painted plasterboard above it
treatment_clinical.ceiling: a suspended grid of white mineral-fibre ceiling tiles, one tile water-stained
treatment_clinical.floor: pale speckled seamless safety vinyl, coved up the wall at the skirting
treatment_clinical.blank: unbroken white glossy wall-cladding sheets below the handrail with satin white painted plasterboard above

ward_bay.why: The ward is the room somebody lies in for a week: warmer paint, a softer floor, the same rail, and the marks of beds parked against the wall.
ward_bay.walls: warm cream painted plaster above the handrail; below it, magnolia wipeable wall-protection sheet with a beige vinyl skirting, dented at bed-frame height
ward_bay.ceiling: plain white painted plasterboard with a recessed curtain track around the bay
ward_bay.floor: marbled beige linoleum, worn dull along the walking line
ward_bay.blank: unbroken magnolia wall-protection sheet below the handrail with warm cream painted plaster above
